skeleton:
Bubble-and-Squeak Eggs Benedict

British · Medium · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Two British institutions in one pan: the leftover mash-and-cabbage cake of Monday morning wearing the poached egg and hollandaise of Sunday brunch. Mini bubble-and-squeak cakes are shaped, fried to a deep golden crust, and used exactly where the English muffin would sit — then the eggs Benedict architecture loads on top. It is the most satisfying kind of recipe: one that makes yesterday's leftovers feel like a decision rather than an economy. The hollandaise here is the blender version taught in full in the black pudding eggs benedict — same quantities, same unbreakable method, restated briefly below. The bubble cake is the new technique of this record: smaller than the whole-pan master, shaped to egg-size, and fried with more butter than the big cake needs because each small cake gets its own crust.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The mini bubble cakes

The poached eggs

The blender hollandaise

full method: black pudding eggs benedict

To finish

  • the full brunch build)
- **The mash and cabbage must be cold and dry** — the same non-negotiables as the bubble-and-squeak master. Fresh-cooked or warm mash makes gluey cakes that never crust. If starting from scratch, boil and chill the potatoes first, or use last night's roast potatoes crushed with the cabbage. - **Chill the shaped cakes 20 minutes** before frying — small cakes are fragile, and the chill is what lets them flip clean. - **Sequence for four warm parts:** cakes fry first (they hold beautifully), bacon next, eggs poach, hollandaise last — it is the one part that cannot wait for anything.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Cakes: chilled before frying, deep-gold crust both faces, steaming hot throughout, centre held at 75 °C for 30 seconds.
  • Eggs: 3-minute poach, towel-drained, yolks domed and liquid.
  • Hollandaise: ribbon-thick, made last, landed within the minute.
  • Assembly order: cake → bacon → egg → sauce, no gaps or slides.

Bubble-and-Squeak Eggs Benedict

Prep: 15 minutes, plus 20 minutes chilling · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 55 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The mini bubble cakes

  • 300 g cold cooked mash (floury potatoes), roughly textured
  • 150 g cold cooked cabbage or Brussels sprouts, squeezed very dry and roughly chopped
  • 20 g unsalted butter, softened
  • 20 g mature Cheddar, grated (optional)
  • 2 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • 20 g butter plus 10 ml neutral oil, for frying

The poached eggs

  • 4 large eggs (220 g), fresh
  • 2 litres water with 30 ml white wine vinegar

The blender hollandaise

  • 3 large egg yolks (55 g)
  • 5 ml lemon juice, plus more to taste
  • 5 ml water
  • 125 g unsalted butter, melted and just bubbling
  • 1 g cayenne, 2 g salt

To finish

  • 6 rashers (300 g) back bacon, grilled or pan-crisped (optional — the full brunch build)
  • 10 g chives, snipped
  • Black pepper

Instructions

  1. **Mix, shape, and chill the cakes.** Mash-mix the potato, cabbage, butter, cheese if using, salt, and pepper with a fork until it holds when squeezed. Shape 4 round cakes — about 110 g each, 8 cm across, 2 cm thick — pressing firmly with a ring or cupped hands to compact them. Chill 20 minutes. Checkpoint — each cake holds a clean edge and lifts off the board without slumping; the surface looks matte and dry. Sticky-shiny means the cabbage is still wet — squeeze again and reshape.
  2. **Fry the cakes to a deep crust, 5 minutes a side.** Heat the 20 g butter and oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low until foaming. Fry the cakes 4–5 minutes the first side, undisturbed, until deep golden, then flip gently and give the second side 4 minutes more. Hold on the warm plates. Checkpoint — both faces are crusty deep gold — darker than you'd dare for a bigger cake, because the small format wants maximum crust — and each cake is steaming hot throughout, with its centre held at 75 °C for 30 seconds on a clean food thermometer. Small cakes brown faster than the master's whole-pan version; medium-low, not medium.
  3. **Bacon, then eggs.** Crisp the bacon in the cakes' pan or under the grill — 4–5 minutes to glassy fat — and hold warm. Slide the eggs into the bare-simmering vinegar water and poach 3 minutes; drain on a towel and trim. Checkpoint — bacon glassy and flat; eggs set-whited, wobbling yolks, dry enough not to slide on their cake.
  4. **The hollandaise, last, 60 seconds.** Yolks, lemon, water, salt, cayenne in the blender — whip 20 seconds — then the bubbling butter in a thin stream with the motor running. Thick, glossy, ribbon stage. Checkpoint — the sauce coats the blade and falls in a slow ribbon; taste and adjust lemon before it leaves the jug. It cannot wait — the eggs are on their cakes within a minute.
  5. **Assemble — cake, bacon, egg, sauce.** A bubble cake, a rasher folded on top if using, the poached egg, and a generous spoon of hollandaise running down the sides. Chives and pepper over. Two plates, landed within the minute. Checkpoint — the cut test: yolk and hollandaise mingling down through the bacon into the cake's crust, and the first forkful is crust, smoke, yolk, and butter-sharp sauce all at once — the leftover plate wearing its Sunday best.

Finish & Plate

This is the brunch plate for the morning after a roast: the cabbage cake doing the muffin's job with more personality, the bacon optional but right, and hollandaise making the whole thing feel like a decision. Tea or fresh coffee, and the honest note that this dish is why you always cook too much mash.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Cakes slumped or fell apartWet cabbage or warm mashSqueeze hard, chill 20 minutes — the master's two rules hold at every size
Pale, soft crustButter not foaming, or heat too lowFoam first; medium-low is gentle, not timid — the crust wants 5 real minutes
Egg slid off the cakeWet egg or cold cakeTowel-drain the egg; the cake fresh from the pan grips
Hollandaise thinButter too cool or poured too fastBlend 10 more seconds; the water-bath hold if plating stalls

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Cakes shaped and chilled:** Refrigerate the mix and use it within 2 days of originally cooking its ingredients. Fry until steaming hot throughout, check the centre holds 75 °C for 30 seconds, and serve straight away; reheat the cooked ingredients only once. Hollandaise never stores; eggs always fresh. - **Variation — the vegetarian build:** skip the bacon, add a grilled tomato and sautéed mushrooms between cake and egg — the plate loses nothing. - **Variation — the crumpet bridge:** half crumpet, half bubble cake, stacked — the full Sunday hybrid for the truly committed. - **The economy loop:** this recipe is the bubble-and-squeak master's brunch descendant — use safely chilled leftover mash within 2 days of its original cooking.

It is the same logic as sauce on a steak: the plate's architecture is built by where the sauce is placed, not where it lands.
